data.title: Tradr Announces Liquidation of SKHA and SKHN
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Tradr ETFs, a provider of ETFs designed for sophisticated investors and professional traders, today announced that a plan of liquidation has been approved for the following funds:

Tradr 2X Long SK hynix Daily ETF (Cboe: SKHA)

Tradr 2X Short SK hynix Daily ETF (Cboe: SKHN)

Each Fund will allow creation and redemption of units through November 5, 2026, which will be the last day of trading on the Cboe BZX Exchange. On or about November 12, 2026, each Fund will cease operations, liquidate assets and prepare to distribute proceeds to shareholders of record.

For detailed information on Tradr ETFs and the significant risks involved with leveraged ETFs, please visit www.tradretfs.com.

About Tradr ETFs

Tradr ETFs are designed for sophisticated investors and professional traders who are looking to express high conviction investment views. The strategies include leveraged and inverse ETFs that seek short or long exposure to actively traded stocks and ETFs.

IMPORTANT RISK INFORMATION

Tradr ETFs are for sophisticated investors and professional traders with high conviction views and are very different from most other ETFs. The Funds are intended to be used as short-term trading vehicles and pursue leveraged investment objectives, which means they are riskier than alternatives that do not use leverage because the Funds magnify the performance of their underlying security. The volatility of the underlying security may affect a Fund's return as much as, or more than, the return of the underlying security.

Investors in the fund should: (a) understand the risks associated with the use of leverage; (b) understand the consequences of seeking inverse and leveraged investment results; (c) for short ETFs, understand the risk of shorting; (d) intend to actively monitor and manage their investment. Fund performance will likely be significantly different than the benchmark over periods longer than the specified reset period and the performance may trend in the opposite direction than its benchmark over periods other than that period.

Leverage increases the risk of a total loss of an investor's investment, may increase the volatility of the Funds, and may magnify any differences between the performance of the Funds and their reference security. The Funds seek leveraged investment results for a specific period (daily, monthly or quarterly). The exact exposure of an investment in the Fund intra-period will depend upon the movement of the reference security from the end of the prior period until the time of investment by the investor.

The Fund will not attempt to position its portfolio to ensure it does not gain or lose more than a maximum percentage of its net asset value on a given trading day. As a consequence, investors in a Fund that seeks two times daily performance would lose all of their money if the Fund's underlying security moves more than 50% in a direction adverse to the Fund on a given trading day.

ETFs involve risk including possible loss of the full principal value. There is no assurance that the Fund will achieve its investment objective. Principal risks and other important risks may be found in the prospectus. Past performance does not guarantee future results.

ETF shares are bought and sold at market price (not NAV) and are not individually redeemed from the ETF. There can be no guarantee that an active trading market for ETF shares will develop or be maintained, or that their listing will continue or remain unchanged. Buying or selling ETF shares on an exchange may require the payment of brokerage commissions and frequent trading may incur brokerage costs that detract significantly from investment returns.

Investors should carefully consider the investment objectives, risks, charges and expenses of the Funds. This and other important information about the Fund is contained in the Prospectus, which can be obtained by visiting www.tradretfs.com. The Prospectus should be read carefully before investing.

data.title: Prediction Markets Now Pose a Win-Win Scenario for Sportsbooks — Market Talk
data.description: Sportsbooks are poised to win out whether or not prediction markets are able to withstand legal challenges from state executive branches, Bank of America analysts Shaun Kelley and Julie Hoover say at the NEXTPredict summit in New York. If prediction markets stick around, the top two sportsbooks, DraftKings and Flutter Entertainment's FanDuel, can offer their own markets with a built-in user base, the analysts say. DraftKings is already the third biggest prediction market exchange, they say. And if prediction markets lose their challenges in court, that will rebuild the competitive mote that DraftKings and FanDuel previously enjoyed, the analysts say. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

data.title: Novartis Says MS Pill Helped Control Disease With Favorable Safety Data in Trials
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Novartis said its experimental multiple sclerosis pill achieved a significant reduction in symptom flare-ups in the most common form of the disease with a favorable safety profile in two late-stage studies.

The Swiss drugmaker said Friday that the studies showed its medicine--known as remibrutinib and marketed as Rhapsido for a skin condition--achieved reductions in the annualized relapse rate of 35.2% and 31.2% compared with Sanofi's Aubagio, meeting the primary goal of both trials.

This translated into one relapse every 13 years, the company said.

No liver safety signal was observed, Novartis said.

Novartis Chief Medical Officer Shreeram Aradhye said the study results point to the drug's potential to support long-term disease management by combining high efficacy with a favorable safety profile.

data.title: Berkshire Stock Is Hot Again. Is It Still a Bargain? — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Andrew Bary

The hottest megacap stock lately has been Berkshire Hathaway, which hit a record high this past week after rising almost 8% in the past month.

Berkshire is probably the ultimate defensive stock, given its diversified earnings power and fortress balance sheet, with over $350 billion in cash, or 30% of its current market value of $1.2 trillion.

So it isn't surprising that Berkshire has rallied as investors rotate out of technology and other artificial-intelligence plays into defensive groups like consumer stocks, real estate, and utilities.

Barron's has been bullish on Berkshire, but the stock doesn't look like a bargain now. The A shares traded Friday at $820,000 after overtaking the old high of about $810,000 set just before the May 2025 annual meeting. The B shares traded at $547. The stock is up 9% this year, still behind the S&P 500's 12% gain.

Berkshire trades for about 1.5 times our estimate of third-quarter book value — the company will probably report results on Nov. 7 — and 24 times projected 2026 operating earnings.

Those aren't excessive, but higher than the average of the past year. What about intrinsic value, Warren Buffett's favorite metric? The stock now trades above UBS analyst Brian Meredith's intrinsic value estimate of $815,000 per A share — one of the higher estimates on Wall Street.

A key issue for Berkshire is its cash deployment. Stock buybacks accelerated in July to over $3 billion, but shares were almost 10% lower then.

Are the buybacks continuing now, given a higher price? And will CEO Greg Abel find plays to invest in? One potential area is the AI space, where capital needs are massive. Berkshire invested $10 billion as part of Alphabet's $85 billion equity capital raise in June, boosting its stake to about $30 billion. Meta Platforms could come to market with a big equity deal by year end, and Berkshire could participate.

Endowment returns are finally beating the S&P 500, and Elon Musk is the reason. Harvard University recently said its endowment rose 27.1% in its fiscal year ending in June — outpacing the S&P's 22% total return. The endowment totaled $68 billion on June 30 — tops among U.S. universities.

SpaceX, which went public in June after a surge in its private-market value in the prior year, was a meaningful contributor to Harvard's strong performance.

Harvard is still trailing the S&P 500 over the past nine years — the tenure of the current endowment leadership — with an 11.4% annual return against 15% for the index.

This year could be tougher for Harvard and its alternatives-heavy portfolio, given the fallout in AI-related stocks. Big endowments have big weightings in private equity and venture capital, but Harvard's alternative allocation is extreme. It has just 14% in public stocks, some 5% in bonds and cash, 46% in private equity and venture capital, and 29% in hedge funds.

There is risk in the stock market, but there may be even greater danger in the Harvard model.

Write to Andrew Bary at andrew.bary@barrons.com

data.title: Bank of Canada to raise rates to 2.50% on October 28 and once again by end-March
data.description:
By Nushaiba Iqbal

The Bank of Canada will raise its overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.50% on October 28 and follow with one more hike by the end of March to pre-empt any further rise in inflation expectations, according to a majority of economists polled by Reuters.

Inflation rose to 3.1% in September, only barely overshooting the BoC's target range of 1% to 3%. But the central bank's latest business outlook survey showed sharply rising inflation expectations in the run-up to a recent breakdown in trade talks with the United States, Canada's main export destination.

Quarterly inflation forecasts from the bank, also due next week, are likely to be revised higher, BoC Governor Tiff Macklem told reporters in remarks Saturday that markets interpreted as a hint a rate rise is coming.

Interest rate futures have moved from pricing in a 30% chance of a rate hike in October to around a three-in-four likelihood. Many economists this week changed their view from a hold to a hike, citing those remarks from Macklem.

"What changed the tone in the governor's public comments on the weekend and what changed our view on Monday is the same source, and that is the responses from the BoC's business outlook and consumer surveys," said Royce Mendes, managing director and head of macro strategy at Desjardins.

"So presumably the governor had seen the results before they were published more broadly on Monday. And I would assume that informed his public commentary," Mendes said. "The survey responses...suggest there are more serious inflationary pressures coming."

Nineteen of 34 economists surveyed in the October 21-23 poll, or 56% of them, said the BoC will hike its overnight rate by a quarter percentage point to 2.50%, its first move in a year.

This is a clear reversal from the previous poll, when 80% of respondents forecast the bank would hold its rate at 2.25% until the end of 2026, and two-thirds of them forecast a hold until the end of March 2027.

Those economists who forecast no move next week mainly cited a weak economy and subdued inflation pressures despite soaring oil prices , which hit $117 a barrel for the first time since May on Friday.

Sixteen of 29 respondents, a 55% majority, also forecast one more rise before March 2027, after which policymakers would hold the overnight rate at 2.75%, poll medians showed. If correct, it will be the shortest BoC policy tightening campaign in 30 years.

But even a short series of hikes would bring the BoC into a widening group of central banks that have opted for tighter monetary policy in response to persistent inflation emerging as a result of the US-led war with Iran that began in February.

Among major central banks, only the BoC and the Bank of England — which is widely expected to raise rates at its early November meeting — have not yet begun to raise rates.

But many say the BoC will need to be measured with the pace of rate increases given other risks to the economy.

Benjamin Reitzes, Canadian rates and macro strategist at BMO, said: "They'd rather make the mistake of hiking a little bit too early, which means maybe they have to hike a little bit less at the end of the day than falling behind the curve, which is what happened in 2021-2022, and they don't want to repeat that mistake.”

Economic growth likely slowed to 1.9% last quarter from 3.3% in Q2 and is forecast at 1.3% in the current one before accelerating next year, poll medians showed. The economy will grow 1.0% in 2026 and 1.7% in 2027, the survey found.

Inflation will average 2.8% for 2026 as a whole, falling to 2.3% in 2027, poll medians showed.

(Other stories from the Reuters global economic poll)

data.title: Western Digital Gets Target Cut Despite Strong Earnings(EDIT1)
data.description:
TD Cowen cut its price target on Western Digital to $430 from $540, but kept a Buy rating after the storage company delivered a strong fiscal first quarter and issued an upbeat outlook.

Analyst Krish Sankar's revised target still implies roughly 21.4% upside from current levels.

The target cut was not driven by weaker demand.

Instead, Sankar lowered the valuation multiple he applies to Western Digital to 15 times earnings from 20 times, reflecting the company's plans to spend more aggressively on capacity expansion.

Western Digital reported $4.38 billion in fiscal Q1 2027 revenue, up 55.3% year over year and above the $4.14 billion consensus estimate.

Adjusted EPS came in at $4.64, beating Wall Street's $4.11 forecast.The company's guidance was even stronger. Western Digital expects $5.80 in EPS for fiscal Q2, roughly 20% above the $4.80 Wall Street had been expecting. Gross margin is projected at 60% to 61%. Sankar sees pricing as the biggest support for the bull case.

Average selling prices are expected to rise by a high-single-digit percentage next quarter and are already up 36% year over year. Most upcoming shipments are covered by long-term agreements, but that has not prevented Western Digital from raising prices.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most important part of TD Cowen's call is that the target cut is really about valuation discipline, not a weakening storage cycle.

Western Digital plans to increase capital spending from roughly $750 million in 2026 to $1.8 billion in 2027 and $2.3 billion in 2028 as it expands supply.

Even then, Sankar expects demand growth for nearline HDDs and enterprise SSDs of roughly 40% to 50% next year, potentially leaving industry supply short of demand.

That matters because HDDs remain dramatically cheaper than NAND storage on a per-terabyte basis.

TD Cowen estimates HDDs could remain 20 to 25 times cheaper per terabyte next year, giving cloud customers an economic incentive to keep buying even if prices rise.

For investors, the key things to watch are HDD pricing, exabyte growth, capex execution, hyperscaler demand and whether margins can stay near current elevated levels.

TD Cowen lowered the multiple.

It did not lower its conviction in the underlying storage cycle.

data.title: Wall Street Firm Cuts Two Hot AI Stock Targets, Picks a Winner
data.description:
Piper Sandler cut its price targets on CoreWeave and Nebius as concerns around AI infrastructure spending, financing and return on invested capital continue to pressure neocloud stocks.

Analyst James Fish lowered his CoreWeave target to $124 from $153, but reiterated a Buy rating and said the stock remains Piper Sandler's preferred name in the AI-as-a-Service space.

He also cut his Nebius target to $185 from $237, while keeping a Hold rating.

The target reductions reflect weaker investor sentiment rather than a collapse in underlying AI demand.

Fish said AI infrastructure stocks could remain in the penalty box until investors see clearer improvement in free cash flow, returns on invested capital and financing visibility.

Still, Piper Sandler believes some of the financing fears surrounding the sector are overdone.

Fish argued that neocloud operators can use customer prepayments and asset-backed debt secured by GPUs to help fund new capacity.

Nebius received prepayments on roughly 70% of deals in Q2 2026, while CoreWeave has historically received prepayments representing about 15% to 25% of total contracted value.

The analyst also pointed to improving operating cash flow at scaled providers and continued support from strategic partners such as Nvidia.

At the same time, GPU-as-a-Service pricing continues to rise, suggesting demand is still running ahead of available supply, although component costs are also climbing.

Investor Takeaway

I think Piper Sandler's call captures the central tension in the neocloud trade.

The demand story still looks strong.

The problem is that investors are becoming much less willing to overlook the huge amount of capital required to satisfy that demand.

CoreWeave remains Piper Sandler's preferred name because Fish believes its assumptions are relatively conservative and its scale gives it better visibility than some earlier-stage competitors.

Nebius, meanwhile, still has attractive cost advantages, but Piper Sandler views it as an earlier-stage story with more execution risk.

For investors, the key things to watch are free cash flow, financing costs, customer prepayments, GPU pricing and whether AI infrastructure companies can turn rapid revenue growth into acceptable returns on capital.

The sector may still have plenty of demand.

But Wall Street increasingly wants proof that the economics can work too.

data.title: BeOne Medicines Says Esophageal Cancer Treatments Had Higher Survival Rates in Phase 3 Study
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

BeOne Medicines said a new combined treatment for esophageal cancer demonstrated an improved overall survival rate in a Phase 3 study.

The oncology company said patients with HER2-positive locally advanced or metastatic gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma who took a combination of Tevimbra and Ziihera, along with chemotherapy, had an overall survival rate of nearly 40% after three years. The median overall survival was 27 months, the company said.

The result was a "sustained" improvement compared with a combination of chemotherapy and trastuzumab, BeOne said.

The company also tested Ziihera and chemotherapy without the addition of Tevimbra. Patients on that regimen had an overall survival rate of 22.9 months, BeOne said, adding that the result was a significant improvement over the control and met the study's primary endpoint.

The company said the additional four months of median survival when adding Tevimbra did not reach statistical significance in the context of an underpowered analysis.

"Following the U.S. approval in August, these longer-term data provide further evidence supporting Tevimbra plus Ziihera and chemotherapy as the new standard of care in all first-line HER2-positive advanced gastroesophageal adenocarcinoma patients, regardless of PD-L1 status," said Mark Lanasa, BeOne's chief medical officer, solid tumors.

Shares of BeOne were down 2% to $374.57 as of late Friday morning.

data.title: Trump's diesel price relief efforts grow costlier as election nears
data.description:
Key points:
  • $8 billion farm aid pushes payments to a record $55.4 billion
  • Analysts see little diesel price relief before midterms
  • Russian fuel deal risks aiding Moscow with little US benefit

By Jarrett Renshaw and Leah Douglas

With the November midterm elections fast approaching, President Donald Trump is throwing an array of costly and politically fraught solutions at one stubborn problem: the price of diesel.

His administration has offered billions of dollars to farmers, relaxed rules for truckers, eased sanctions on Russian fuel and pressured European allies to release emergency stocks. Yet diesel prices rose again last week, leaving Trump spending political and financial capital without delivering the relief his party wants as voters go to the polls.

Republicans are defending narrow majorities in Congress, and high costs are a major concern for voters. Nearly 80% of Americans blame Trump for higher costs, according to an October Reuters/Ipsos poll.

US diesel prices rose nearly 10 cents a gallon in the latest week to an average of $6.28, reversing two weeks of declines and remaining near record highs, according to the Energy Information Administration.

The political pressure is particularly acute in traditionally Republican Farm Belt states like Iowa and Kansas, where rising fuel and fertilizer costs, trade disruptions and weak farm economics have fueled discontent among some of Trump's core supporters.

Trump has promoted his diesel measures at campaign rallies across the region. He signed an executive order onstage in Nebraska allowing red-dyed diesel to be used in highway vehicles and announced $8 billion in new farm aid during a rally in Kansas on Monday.

The measures illustrate the trade-offs Trump is accepting in pursuit of near-term relief. The new aid adds fresh strain on federal spending, while the Russian fuel move risks helping Moscow finance its war in Ukraine. Pressure on European allies to release emergency stocks, backed by a threat to restrict US diesel exports, has created diplomatic friction.

“The president tends to discount long-term losses over short-term gain, and I am skeptical if there is any short gain to be had here,” said Chris Borick, a pollster and political scientist at Muhlenberg College in Pennsylvania.

The White House attributed high diesel prices to “pre-existing issues,” including years of refinery closures and damage from Russia's war in Ukraine, while defending Trump's efforts to ease costs.

“The President wants diesel prices to fall, which is why he has taken historic actions to save American farmers, truckers, and workers every hard-earned penny," White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers said.

SKEPTICISM AND UNANSWERED QUESTIONS

One of Trump's most direct attempts to lower diesel costs has struggled to gain traction.

Trump signed an executive order this month allowing truckers to use red-dyed diesel, typically intended for off-road use such as farm equipment, for highway driving while temporarily avoiding certain federal tax reporting and record-keeping requirements.

But the IRS has not eliminated the federal diesel tax, instead temporarily waiving related reporting requirements and penalties through year-end, leaving uncertainty for truck stops and fuel sellers.

David Fialkov, top lobbyist at NATSO, a trade group representing the largest US truck stop operators, said members appreciate Trump's effort to tackle diesel costs but that the guidance remains "murky" and carries too much risk.

"I really don’t see any of these dyed diesel announcements making a meaningful dent in diesel prices," Fialkov said.

Trump is also turning to federal payments to cushion some of the constituencies feeling the pain.

Government payments to farmers were already expected to top $47 billion this year, buoyed by commodity payments and $12 billion in tariff relief distributed by the US Department of Agriculture earlier this year. The $8 billion farm relief program would push the total to a record $55.4 billion, exceeding the previous high of $45 billion in 2020, when farmers received pandemic assistance.

The payments can help farmers manage higher costs and lost sales but do not directly address the market disruptions driving up fuel and fertilizer prices. They also raise questions about taxpayer spending to compensate producers for damage that farm groups say is linked partly to the administration’s own trade and foreign policies.

“This is the second round of emergency aid this year to address losses that were largely foreseeable,” National Farmers Union President Rob Larew said. “Trade disruptions and rising fuel costs tied to conflict abroad have put family farmers in a difficult position, and one-time payments can't provide the stability they need to plan for the future.”

The aid will arrive after the November 3 election, and likely not reach farmers until the end of the year, USDA official Richard Fordyce told Reuters on Friday.

FRICTION OVER RUSSIAN FUEL

Some of Trump's efforts to increase diesel supplies carry geopolitical trade-offs.

His decision to ease sanctions on Russian diesel that were designed to restrict Moscow’s energy revenues and limit its ability to finance its war in Ukraine has drawn bipartisan criticism — and raised questions about whether the move will meaningfully lower US fuel prices.

Trump has defended the sanctions relief as necessary to draw Russian President Vladimir Putin into negotiations to end the war in Ukraine and to release American prisoner Stephen Hubbard.

As the administration's intervention efforts have failed to lower fuel costs, Trump has sought to shift blame toward Ukraine and President Volodymyr Zelenskiy rather than the Iran war ahead of the elections.

Analysts say the Iran conflict has been the much bigger driver of the diesel price spike, disrupting global oil flows and refined-fuel supplies, while Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries have helped tighten supplies but played a more limited role in the price.

“I sort of see it as a blame-shifting kind of scapegoating operation, more than a genuine attempt to moderate prices in the lead-up to the election,” said Edward Fishman, director of the Maurice R. Greenberg Center at the Council on Foreign Relations.

data.title: SLB Revenue Rises as Data-Center Demand Grows, Middle East Business Recovers — Update
data.description:
By Connor Hart

SLB notched higher revenue in the recent quarter, supported by rapid growth in its data-center division and a gradual recovery in its Middle East business.

Chief Executive Olivier Le Peuch said demand for artificial intelligence is driving unprecedented investment in data-center infrastructure. In turn, SLB is expanding its capabilities to capitalize on that demand, including through its planned $4.1 billion acquisition of thermal-management company Kelvion and the recent buildout of a manufacturing center in Canada.

"We continue to strengthen our position as an industrial technology partner to the data-center industry and to expand our participation in this rapidly growing market," Le Peuch said on a call with analysts Friday.

Shares were recently trading 6.6% higher, at $52.84, up more than 31% year to date.

SLB's third-quarter revenue climbed 5.8% to $9.45 billion, ahead of analyst estimates. The increase was driven in part by its data-center solutions business, as revenue jumped 23% sequentially amid growing demand, an expanding range of services and geographic expansion into Asia.

At the same time, Le Peuch said each of SLB's core divisions is growing: "This was driven by the gradual recovery in the Middle East, solid growth in North America and continued momentum across the international offshore basins, including Latin America, Europe and Africa and Asia."

SLB's business in the Middle East grew 13% sequentially, despite some disruptions late in the quarter, Le Peuch said. Overall, international revenue ticked up 1% to $6.99 billion, while North American revenue jumped 24% to $2.4 billion.

The oilfield-services company, formerly known as Schlumberger, posted a profit of $735 million, or 49 cents a share, for its three months ended Sept. 30, compared with $739 million, or 50 cents a share, a year earlier. On an adjusted basis, quarterly earnings came in at 64 cents a share, ahead of the 62 cents a share that analysts surveyed by FactSet expected.

Looking ahead, SLB expects global oilfield-services activity to grow by a mid-single-digit percentage in 2027, supported by offshore developments, renewed exploration activity and investments in production and recovery.

The outlook assumes Middle East activity remains at second-half 2026 levels and that regional tensions don't escalate further, Le Peuch said. A normalization of activity in the region could unlock deferred projects and provide additional upside to growth.

data.title: NYMEX Overview: Petroleum Futures Rise For Second Day as Mideast Tensions Remain High — OPIS
data.description:
Crude oil and refined product futures prices were seeing a second day of solid increases Friday as escalating tensions in the Middle East had most contracts ending the week with gains.

U.S. crude prices were back above the $100/bbl mark at 11:15 a.m. ET, with the December West Texas Intermediate crude contract trading $2.81 higher to $102.28/bbl, a change of 2.8%.

January WTI prices were up by $2.76 to $100.28/bbl.

Brent crude prices were seeing similar proportional increases, with December Brent rising by $3.03 to $116.20/bbl and the January contract ahead by $2.68 to $111.34/bbl.

RBOB futures were leading products higher, with the November contract ahead by 4.15cts to $3.2180/gal, a gain of 1.4%. December prices were rising by 4.48cts to $3.1341/gal.

ULSD increases were under 0.5%, with the November contract moving up by 2.72cts to $4.9593/gal and December prices rising by 2.7cts to $4.7636/gal.

The gains come as tensions continue to increase in the Persian Gulf region, with the U.S. and Israel reportedly preparing to resume strikes on Iran and Iranian leaders threatening to retaliate by striking civilian targets in the region.

"The physical market is more balanced than the headlines suggest. Gulf oil exports have recovered significantly in recent weeks, which gives the market some protection, while emergency stock releases have also helped ease immediate supply fears," said Zaheer Anwari, founder of The Revacy Fund, in an analysis Friday. "That does not remove the risk. Shipping through the region remains disrupted, freight and insurance costs are still elevated and any fresh attack on energy infrastructure could quickly tighten supply again."

data.title: Hears Everything, Uploads Nothing: VoxNexus Launches Android's First Low-Power On-Device Always-On Voice Artificial Intelligence (AI)
data.description:
VoxNexus AI/ Key word(s): Product Launch

Hears Everything, Uploads Nothing: VoxNexus Launches Android's First Low-Power On-Device Always-On Voice Artificial Intelligence (AI)

23.10.2026 / 17:55 CET/CEST

The issuer is solely responsible for the content of this announcement.

VoxNexus’ new on-device ambient listening solution runs for 12 hours on 2.49% of a phone's battery and never sends audio to the cloud

MADRID, Spain, October 23, 2026/APO Group/ -- VoxNexus (www.VoxNexus.ai) released VoxEdge, an on-device voice stack that brings speech recognition, translation and speech synthesis to affordable Android devices, entirely offline. VoxEdge supports speech recognition in 36 languages, translation in 103 languages, and speech synthesis in 45 languages—all running with no connection, no data bundle, and no cloud token bills.

AI should work for everyone, not just for speakers of a handful of mainstream languages. Yet across much of Africa, voice AI has been held back by scarce training data and the lack of targeted fine-tuning. Everyday speech also includes code-switching and dialect variation, while cloud-based inference costs can make deployment at scale expensive.

VoxNexus’s solutions run entirely on device, and every query is free once the model is installed on the device. Its speech recognition model has as few as 65 million parameters and achieves a lower word error rate than open-source models nearly ten times its size.

“Under-resource languages aren’t small languages. Hundreds of millions of people speak them. Until now, AI models just haven’t learned them yet,” said Charles Shi, CEO of VoxNexus.

VoxNexus also launched VoxSense, an on-device ambient listening solution that uses only 162 mAh for 12 hours of continuous listening, around 2.5% of a 6,500 mAh phone battery. By keeping all processing on device, VoxSense makes always-on listening practical without draining the battery and without sending any audio to the cloud. Developers and device makers can easily integrate it through a license and a simple SDK. Developers can request a free trial here: www.VoxNexus.ai.

VoxSense and VoxEdge were unveiled at the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 launch in Madrid on October 19.

VoxNexus builds AI that hears and speaks — for everyone, everywhere, all the time. data.title: USO Jumps To Over 11-Year High As Brent Tops $116, WTI Crosses $100 Amid Escalating Middle East Tensions
data.description:
Key points:
  • Iran’s army chief Maj. Gen. Amir Hatami said the military is fully prepared for “asymmetric warfare,” amid speculation of renewed U.S. strikes.
  • Citi cautioned the rebound in Strait of Hormuz shipments may not last, as stronger flows could reflect inventory drawdowns or released stockpiles.
  • UBS warned further escalation could renew supply disruptions, with volatile flows and high freight rates leaving the market undersupplied.

The United States Oil Fund (USO) jumped to hit its highest level in more than 11 years as crude prices rallied amid escalating Middle East tensions and concerns over potential supply disruptions.

USO, which tracks movements in U.S. crude oil futures, touched $167.88, its highest level since May 2015, according to historical price data.

Brent crude futures maturing in December climbed 2.63% to $116.15 per barrel on Friday, hitting a six-month high, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures for the same month gained 2.95% to $102.40 per barrel.

Saudi Attacks, Iran Tensions Raise Oil Supply Concerns

Oil prices extended their gains as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia intensified concerns over the security of energy infrastructure and shipments across the Middle East.

Saudi Aramco instructed employees to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters and work remotely on Thursday, Reuters reported, following attacks in the country's eastern oil-producing region.

Iran's army chief, Maj. Gen. Amir Hatami, said Thursday that the country's military was fully prepared for “asymmetric warfare,” according to state news agency Tasnim. The developments come amid speculation about renewed U.S. strikes on Iran.

The comments come after President Donald Trump said Wednesday that Washington was not negotiating with Tehran and suggested further developments could follow soon. Brent futures were on track for a third consecutive weekly gain as traders assessed the potential for further escalation.

Citi Warns Gulf Oil Export Recovery May Be Temporary

Despite Brent crude rising more than 85% this year, Bloomberg reported that oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered toward pre-war levels.

Citigroup analysts, including Francesco Martoccia, cautioned that the recent improvement in shipments may not represent a sustained recovery, as stronger flows could reflect inventory drawdowns or the release of previously stockpiled oil.

UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo told Reuters that further escalation could trigger renewed supply disruptions, with volatile oil flows and elevated freight rates leaving the market undersupplied.

What Retail Thinks About USO

On Stocktwits, retail investors’ sentiment around USO remained in the ‘bullish’ territory over the past day amid ‘high’ message volume levels.

So far this year, USO has rallied over 145%. Meanwhile, the ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil (UCO), which seeks twice the daily performance of a WTI crude oil futures index, has surged nearly 242% over the same period.
